bio:
Montréal singer-songwriter Sam Roberts broke nationally after years in local bands with the 2002 EP The Inhuman Condition. “Brother Down” and “Don't Walk Away Eileen” gave Canadian radio a guitar-driven sound that drew equally from classic rock, folk songwriting and Britpop, setting up the 2003 full-length We Were Born in a Flame. The album debuted at No. 2 in Canada, eventually went double platinum and made Roberts one of the country's defining rock newcomers of the early 2000s.

We Were Born in a Flame won three JUNO Awards, including Album of the Year, Rock Album of the Year and Artist of the Year. Roberts followed it with Chemical City and the JUNO-winning Love at the End of the World, then increasingly worked under the Sam Roberts Band name as the project settled into a durable group identity. Later albums retained the direct choruses and guitar foundation while opening toward psychedelic rock, groove-oriented arrangements and more expansive production.

Roberts occupies an important middle ground in Canadian rock: successful enough to become a national radio staple, but rooted in a Montréal band culture and album-oriented sensibility that kept the work from feeling manufactured around singles alone. Songs such as “Brother Down” became part of the country's 2000s rock vocabulary, while the band's longevity carried that audience across multiple generations of Canadian alternative radio.

Sam-r is a Syrian-born, Toronto-based hip-hop artist, producer and multi-instrumentalist who arrived in Canada as a refugee in 2017. He has built his career in Toronto through solo releases, live-band performance and The Cook-Up Sessions, a collaborative series he launched in 2023. His Northern Dial library credits span Death of a Saint, Aura, The Cook-Up Sessions Vol. 1 and later singles including Dystopia.

Sara is a split library credit for Sara Quin of the Canadian duo Tegan and Sara. Calgary-born twin sisters Sara and Tegan Quin built an internationally acclaimed career spanning indie rock, alternative pop and synth-pop, with records including The Con, Sainthood, Heartthrob and Love You to Death.

Burlington-born Sarah Harmer first built a reputation in Ontario's independent rock community with Weeping Tile before moving toward a solo career at the end of the 1990s. Her 2000 album You Were Here became the breakthrough, pairing intimate songwriting with understated folk-rock arrangements on songs such as "Basement Apt." and "Lodestar." Rather than treating singer-songwriter music as separate from the Canadian indie-rock network around her, Harmer carried the community and collaborative sensibility of her band years into a quieter solo vocabulary.

All of Our Names and the roots-oriented I'm a Mountain expanded that catalogue, with the latter emerging partly from Harmer's I Love the Escarpment tour. The project connected music directly to her campaign against development threats around Ontario's Niagara Escarpment, making environmental advocacy an unusually concrete part of her artistic life. She returned to a fuller electric sound on Oh Little Fire before stepping away from album releases for much of the 2010s while remaining active in environmental work.

Are You Gone arrived in 2020 after a decade between studio albums and deliberately reconnected personal songwriting with questions about climate, place and civic responsibility. Harmer's importance in Canadian music comes from the consistency of those connections: Ontario geography, independent-rock community, folk tradition and environmental activism are not separate chapters in her career but overlapping parts of the same body of work.

Canadian multidisciplinary artist Sarah Swire is a singer-songwriter, actor, choreographer and writer who records art-rock under her own name and as Sister Swire. Raised in Canada with Ottawa Valley roots, she later studied at the Royal Conservatoire of Scotland and returned to Canada to record her 2023 debut album with Joel Plaskett in Dartmouth, Nova Scotia.
city: Ottawa Valley, Ontario / Dartmouth, Nova Scotia

bio: Sargeant is Calgary vocalist Yolanda Sargeant, one half of the acclaimed lo-fi soul duo Sargeant X Comrade. Her expressive vocals sit at the centre of the group's blend of soul, hip-hop, funk and sample-driven production. Northern Dial carries Sargeant as part of its Calgary and Western Canadian soul catalogue.

Ottawa-born and Toronto-rooted rapper, singer and producer Saukrates is one of the architects of modern Canadian hip-hop. He began releasing music in the mid-1990s, co-founded Capitol Hill Music and built a reputation as both an MC and producer at a time when Canadian rap artists had few durable routes to major-label support. His early single "Still Caught Up" earned a JUNO nomination, and his 1999 debut The Underground Tapes became an influential document of Toronto's late-1990s underground.

Saukrates' career has always moved between roles. He signed major-label deals, worked as a producer and collaborator, and expanded into R&B as part of Big Black Lincoln. His credits and collaborations connect him to Redman, Nas, Nelly Furtado, k-os, Classified, Maestro Fresh Wes and other major figures, while his mentorship also mattered behind the scenes: producer Boi-1da has cited Saukrates as an early supporter who helped open doors in Toronto's music community.

Later releases including Season One, Season 2 and the long-delayed Bad Addiction extended a catalogue that spans boom-bap, melodic rap and R&B. More than a conventional solo career, Saukrates represents the connective tissue of Canadian hip-hop: an artist, producer and mentor whose influence runs through several generations of Toronto music.

Québec-born country singer Savannah Jade is a Canadian artist whose solo career followed her work in the duo Five Roses and blends polished contemporary country with a performance background in figure skating.
Scarborough R&B singer-songwriter Savannah Ré is a multi-Juno-winning Canadian artist known for intimate, emotionally candid songwriting and collaborations across contemporary R&B.
Toronto producer, rapper and engineer Savilion is a Canadian underground hip-hop artist whose career spans the group Creature Box, solo releases, production work and membership in Swamp Thing.

Sawan Kanota, professionally known as savvan, is a Canadian producer, multi-instrumentalist, saxophonist, music director and film composer from the Greater Toronto Area. Working across R&B, pop and hip-hop, he combines Western and Eastern musical traditions through production, performance and engineering. His production and performance on Divine Lightbody's 2025 track nightlife is his Northern Dial library credit.
Toronto-born multi-instrumentalist Saya Gray is a Canadian experimental pop artist whose music blends alternative pop, R&B, jazz-trained musicianship and densely layered production.

St. Catharines rapper Sayzee, formerly known as Sese, is a Canadian underground hip-hop artist known for intricate lyricism, anime references and the long-running Your Favourite Rapper's Worst Nightmare series.

Sazon Diamante was an East Vancouver rapper and an early Latin voice in Canadian hip-hop. A childhood friend and collaborator of Concise and the younger brother of Rascalz producer DJ Kemo, he appeared with the Rascalz and Notch on the 2002 single Crazy World before his death, leaving a lasting connection to Vancouver's hip-hop history.

key: scifo of the micn gz crew
display_name: Scifo of the Micn Gz Crew
bio: Scifo, born Andil Houlder, is a Toronto rapper best known as one half of the Canadian hip-hop duo Mic'N Gz Crew. The group emerged from Toronto's early-1990s rap scene and released All Chix Lov Da Mix through the Canadian label Def Beat Records. Northern Dial carries Scifo through his later guest appearance on 2 Versatile's 'Guiding Light.'

Toronto singer-songwriter Scott Helman broke nationally while still in his teens, with the Augusta EP establishing the conversational writing and polished folk-pop sound that would become his foundation. "Bungalow" became a platinum Canadian single, turning an early radio introduction into a durable audience and helping Helman move quickly from emerging-artist status into national touring and awards recognition.

The 2017 album Hôtel de Ville widened his sound without abandoning the compact songwriting that drove the breakthrough. "PDA" earned gold certification, while the later Hang Ups EP produced another gold title track. Across this period, Helman accumulated seven JUNO nominations and toured with artists including Tegan and Sara, Shawn Mendes, Vance Joy, Walk Off the Earth and Dean Lewis, placing him firmly inside the generation of Canadian singer-songwriters who developed through both radio and festival circuits.

Helman's second album Nonsuch Park (sa) pushed the writing toward adulthood, anxiety and changing relationships, with "Wait No More" becoming another gold single. He has also used his platform for environmental advocacy, including the Evergreen Manuscript and MayDay initiatives around climate action. Helman's significance is less about one dramatic crossover than sustained Canadian pop craftsmanship: a decade-plus catalogue of accessible songs that repeatedly connected introspective writing to mainstream radio without flattening his personality.

Toronto rapper Scotty IV is a Canadian MC and member of the Stay Out Late collective whose introspective writing draws on experiences ranging from university and homelessness to survival and personal growth. His solo catalogue and group work have connected him with artists including Tremayne, Noyz and Kardinal Offishall, who featured him on the Canadian posse cut One For All (Remix).
Toronto singer-songwriter Sean Jones is a Canadian R&B vocalist who first broke through with the Juno-winning group In Essence before developing a solo career rooted in classic soul.
Toronto rapper, singer and producer Sean Leon is a Canadian hip-hop artist and founder of the IXXI Initiative, known for experimental solo work and songwriting collaborations.

Seb C is a Vancouver-based house DJ and producer active in British Columbia's electronic music scene. His work is centred on club-focused house music, DJ performance and independent releases. Northern Dial carries Seb C as part of its Canadian electronic and dance catalogue.
Mississauga-born musician, singer, songwriter and producer Sebastien Grainger is a Canadian artist best known as the vocalist and drummer of dance-punk duo Death From Above 1979.

Halifax duo Sebutones was an early Canadian experimental hip-hop project formed by Buck 65 and Sixtoo, pushing the city's 1990s underground rap scene toward abstract production and left-field lyricism.
Montréal-formed, Toronto-based band See Spot Run is a Canadian rock group known for independent radio success, extensive national touring and the hit single Weightless.

Vancouver artist, songwriter and producer Sekawnee Baker is an Afro-Indigenous musician from the Squamish, Tla'amin, Kwakwaka'wakw/Musgamagw Dzawada'enuxw, Tlingit and Haida Nations. Working across hip-hop, R&B and production, he has developed his own catalogue while also creating recording opportunities for young artists in Vancouver.

SepTo is a Toronto hip-hop artist whose work emerged from the city's independent rap scene in the early 2010s. His catalogue includes projects such as T.O for Toronto and Almost NevR, along with collaborations with Korry Deez, Dan-e-o and Rich Kidd; his appearance on Dan-e-o's Get Up On It is the track represented in the Northern Dial library.

Raised near Peterborough, Ontario, Serena Ryder developed from a roots-oriented singer-songwriter into one of Canada's most durable crossover voices. Early records established her in folk and acoustic music, while If Your Memory Serves You Well and Is It O.K. widened her national audience. Her powerful, flexible voice became the constant as she moved between folk, rock, soul and pop rather than settling into a single format.

The major commercial turn came with Harmony in 2012. "Stompa" and "What I Wouldn't Do" brought Ryder to a much larger radio audience, and the record helped drive a dominant 2014 JUNO year in which she won Artist of the Year and Songwriter of the Year. Across her career she has accumulated seven JUNO wins, placing her among the more decorated Canadian artists of her generation. Later releases including Utopia continued her pop-rock expansion without erasing the roots foundation underneath it.

Ryder's 2021 album The Art of Falling Apart brought mental health, recovery and self-examination closer to the centre of her writing and won the 2022 JUNO for Adult Contemporary Album of the Year. Her career matters in Canadian music because it connects several ecosystems that are often treated separately: the singer-songwriter circuit, roots music, commercial rock and adult pop. Rather than a single breakthrough defining her, Ryder has repeatedly reshaped the setting around a voice that remains immediately recognizable.

Set2 is a Canadian hip-hop artist associated with Toronto independent label Motive Music Canada. His catalogue includes releases and collaborations with Gee Wunder and Mezziah, with Motive projects receiving Canadian college and commercial radio play and Set2 continuing to appear on Toronto rap releases into the 2020s.

Toronto-based Canadian rapper Seth Dyer built momentum through a prolific independent release schedule and playlist breakthroughs, with tracks including What You Need helping expand his audience during the Dyer Days project.

Born in Kenya to Rwandan parents and raised in London, Ontario, Shadrach Kabango built one of Canadian hip-hop's most respected careers through a combination of technical lyricism, humour, social observation and unusually reflective writing. His early albums established him outside the dominant commercial rap lane, while The Old Prince became a breakthrough and helped position him as a major voice in Canadian independent hip-hop.

Shad followed with TSOL and Flying Colours, records that deepened his reputation for writing about identity, immigration, relationships, faith and public life without sacrificing playfulness or craft. He has been repeatedly recognized by the Polaris Music Prize and won the JUNO Award for Rap Recording of the Year, while collaborations with artists including Lights, k-os and Saukrates connect his catalogue to several strands of Canadian music.

His cultural reach expanded further through broadcasting. As host of the documentary series Hip-Hop Evolution, Shad helped tell the history of the genre to an international audience, bringing the same curiosity and contextual thinking that define his songwriting. That combination of acclaimed records and music-history work has made him an important bridge between Canadian rap as a creative practice and hip-hop as a broader culture.
Montréal trio Shades of Culture is a pioneering Canadian hip-hop group whose English-language rap and turntablism helped establish Québec hip-hop beyond the province in the 1990s.

Toronto MC, producer and vocalist Shakari Nyte is a Canadian artist best known for work with the R&B and hip-hop supergroup Big Black Lincoln alongside Saukrates, T.R.A.C.K.S., Agile and Ro Dolla. His credits also include collaboration with Esthero on Wikked Lil' Grrrls, where Billboard identified him among the album's Canadian contributors.

Scarborough MC Rishaard, also credited as Shamon Harage, is a member of the long-running Canadian hip-hop collective Monolith. His recorded work includes appearances alongside Dan-e-o, Wio-K, Grimace Love and other Monolith members on records including The Book of Daniel, In Real Life and Perception.

Shanks Sioux is an Indigenous hip-hop artist whose work is connected to Canada's West Coast rap scene. He has appeared on Snotty Nose Rez Kids releases including I Can't Remember My Name and Cops With Guns Are The Worst!!!, and the former was recognized among the finalists at the Canadian Independent Music Video Awards. Northern Dial carries Shanks Sioux as part of its Indigenous Canadian hip-hop catalogue.
Toronto-born R&B singer-songwriter Shantel May pairs soulful vocals with contemporary production and candid relationship writing across a growing independent catalogue.
Toronto-born rapper ShaqIsDope is a Canadian hip-hop artist whose introspective lyricism and polished independent releases grew from the city's competitive underground rap scene.
Canadian rapper, speaker and educator Shaun Boothe uses hip-hop storytelling in music and his Unauthorized Biography Series, turning the lives of cultural figures into narrative rap performances.

Mississauga-born Shawn Desman spent years performing in Portuguese-language music before becoming one of the defining Canadian pop-R&B performers of the early 2000s. His 2002 English-language debut Shawn Desman arrived with "Get Ready," "Shook" and "Spread My Wings," combining R&B vocals, hip-hop-influenced production and choreography at a time when Canadian radio had relatively few homegrown male artists working in that lane. The album went gold and established Desman as both a singer and a performance-focused pop act.

Back for More strengthened that position and won the JUNO for R&B/Soul Recording of the Year. Desman then successfully adapted to the dance-pop shift of the late 2000s and early 2010s with Fresh, whose singles "Shiver," "Electric" and "Night Like This" became some of his biggest records. "Night Like This" reached No. 1 in Canada, while its choreography-heavy video helped Desman win Video of the Year at the MuchMusic Video Awards. The later album Alive extended his interest in connecting pop songs with visual storytelling through an accompanying scripted film.

After stepping away from music for family reasons, Desman returned to a much warmer reception than he expected, including a prominent appearance during Drake's 2022 OVO Fest celebration of Canadian hip-hop and R&B. That comeback reframed his catalogue as part of a larger Canadian pop history. Desman's importance lies in how he occupied the space between R&B, dance music, choreography and mainstream radio before those combinations became routine in Canadian pop.

Raised in rural British Columbia, Shawn Hook developed first as a multi-instrumentalist and songwriter, studying piano and later audio engineering before his own pop career accelerated. Early releases under his birth name preceded his transition to Shawn Hook and the 2012 album Cosmonaut and the Girl, where electronic and dance-pop elements began to replace the more acoustic sound of his first recordings. His experience writing music for television also gave him a practical songwriting background before Canadian radio became the centre of his career.

The 2015 album Analog Love produced "Sound of Your Heart," the song that brought Hook his widest international exposure and became a multi-platinum Canadian single. He followed with "Reminding Me," a duet with Vanessa Hudgens that also achieved major Canadian certification, while My Side of Your Story extended the polished pop direction. Across this period Hook earned multiple JUNO nominations, appeared on major U.S. television and accumulated hundreds of millions of streams, moving a British Columbia songwriter into a genuinely cross-border pop audience.

Canada's Walk of Fame recognized Hook with the Allan Slaight Music Impact Honour in 2017, an award aimed at young Canadian artists making an international impact. Later releases included collaborations such as "Used To You" with Serena Ryder and, after treatment for cancer in 2023, the 2024 project Beauty in Surrender marked another personal and professional return. Hook's career is best understood as a long songwriting progression rather than a single-hit story: regional beginnings, television composition, national radio and international pop all feed into the same catalogue.
Two-Spirit Mohawk singer-songwriter Shawnee Kish is an award-winning Canadian artist known for powerhouse vocals and identity-rooted songwriting.
Montréal-based singer-songwriter Shay Lia pairs soulful vocals with danceable alternative R&B and has frequently collaborated with Kaytranada.

Shaye was a Canadian pop and folk-rock group formed by established singer-songwriters Kim Stockwood, Damhnait Doyle and Tara MacLean, with a catalogue built around close harmonies and melodic songwriting.

Halifax-born, Toronto-based indie-pop singer-songwriter SHEAL, the stage name of Sheilagh McNab, makes piano-led songs built around intimate writing and emotive vocals. Her releases include the golden hours EP and the home-going project, while her music has received national CBC radio play and collaborations with Canadian artists including Eternia, Rel McCoy and Shad.

Shelailai is a Canadian-Caribbean rapper and pop artist who emerged from Vancouver before expanding her career into the United States. Her music moves between hip-hop, pop and Caribbean-influenced sounds, with an independent catalogue built across both sides of the border. Northern Dial carries Shelailai as part of its Canadian hip-hop and pop catalogue.
Toronto singer-songwriter Shi Wisdom is a Canadian neo-soul and R&B vocalist known for expressive, classically informed singing and songwriting credits for artists including Rita Ora.
Abbotsford-born singer-songwriter Shiloh Hoganson, now known as Lyldoll, is a Canadian pop-punk and alternative-pop artist whose 2009 debut album reached Canada's Top 10.

Shog Stan is an Ottawa-based hip-hop artist and producer who writes, performs, produces and engineers his own releases. His recent catalogue includes the 2026 album Mr.ShogStan and singles such as 'I Gotta' and 'What You Saying.' Northern Dial carries Shog Stan as part of its contemporary Ottawa independent hip-hop catalogue.
Mohawk producer and turntablist Shub, formerly known as DJ Shub, is a Six Nations artist and former A Tribe Called Red member who helped pioneer the powwow-step sound.

Scarborough hip-hop group Sic Sense formed in the mid-1990s around members Dub ILL, 6Pak and Boom, becoming part of Toronto's independent boom-bap scene through records including Positional Bypass and Onemantality.

Toronto-born and raised singer, songwriter and composer Simar is a Canadian Punjabi artist blending hip-hop, R&B and pop with Punjabi-language songwriting. She has collaborated with artists including Sidhu Moosewala, Fateh and Talwiinder while building a bilingual catalogue that places a female perspective at the centre of contemporary Punjabi music.

Toronto-born vocalist Simone Denny is a Canadian dance and house singer best known as the voice of Love Inc., BKS and Widelife and for enduring club hits including You're a Superstar and Broken Bones.
